quotes.text: GPAgentBench-2K was constructed using real-world GP visit records from a primary-care network.

rationale: The source is named as real-world GP visit records from a primary-care network. The packet does not report a time frame, platform, version/snapshot date for source data, or a route from each task to a source record.

quotes.text: GPAgentBench-2K is under a non-commercial research-use license.
The information you provide in this study will be used only for academic research.

rationale: The paper states data origin and collection from real GP records, plus licence terms. It also documents consent language for human evaluators and data handling.

quotes.text: male patients account for 57.6% and females for 42.4% of the 2,256 cases with recorded gender data.

rationale: The appendix reports descriptive statistics for demographics, specialties, symptoms, exams, and tests. It does not compare these features against a named target population.

quotes.text: The safety cost captures two types of management errors: (1) Missed Referral (Miss Refer)

rationale: The benchmark includes dedicated safety metrics and reports unsafe management errors. The packet does not show a dedicated bias test.

quotes.text: We evaluate off-the-shelf LLMs on a 20% random test split stratified by management label

rationale: A held-out random test split is reported, which is a developer-side control. The packet does not report a measured contamination or overlap check.

quotes.text: the ground-truth diagnosis and disposition is hidden from the agent.

rationale: The paper states that ground truth is hidden from the agent. It does not name a concrete runtime isolation mechanism such as no mount, no credential, no network path, or non-public labels.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet names live model APIs, simulator and judge model families, but does not pin data, software, simulator, or judge snapshots as a frozen reproducible environment.

quotes.text: collected cases undergo rigorous validation by two senior physicians.

rationale: Physician validation of cases is manual solvability/correctness evidence. There is no scripted oracle reference solution run through the grader with reported result.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The benchmark has stateful trajectories, but the packet does not report checks that unchanged or irrelevant state remains unaffected.

quotes.text: The agent must generate XML-style tags

rationale: The benchmark reports structured XML-style actions, action masking, terminal management decisions, and detailed clinical scoring, which is a design argument against trivial success. It does not report an empirical random or trivial-agent success rate.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The reported baselines are LLMs and RL methods, not a do-nothing or random agent.

quotes.text: The averaged Cohen’s \kappa between GPT-5.4 judge and physicians is 0.92 for Dx accuracy and 0.89 for Tx score.

rationale: The benchmark validates its automatic judge on sampled outputs from its own evaluated models. It reports agreement figures against two senior physicians.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet does not report seeds, temperature-zero decoding, or a repeated-run policy.

quotes.text: Parentheses report the standard error of the mean.

rationale: Headline tables report standard errors. The packet uses language such as significant degradation, but it does not report a statistical test or CI for the headline model comparison.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet gives numbers of cases and sampled audit outputs, but not the number of runs per task behind each headline score. It also does not state seed/sampling policy or run independence for headline scores.

quotes.text: mean \pm standard error across test cases.

rationale: The appendix reports standard error and states that it is across test cases. Clustering of tasks within patients, templates, or groups is not addressed.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. There is no rerun reliability metric for actions, final state, or pass^k-style all-runs outcomes.

quotes.text: GPT-5.4 OpenAI (2026)

rationale: Some evaluated models are named with years, satisfying the model identifier/date element. Decoding parameters and a harness version or commit matching reported results are not reported.

quotes.text: The agent must generate XML-style tags

rationale: The benchmark defines a text-command action interface, so NA does not apply. It reports XML-style tags and required fields, but does not document side effects per tool or full return/error semantics; no S5 chunks are present.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The benchmark defines a text-command action interface, so NA does not apply. The packet does not report tool conformance tests, simulated/no-op tool disclosure, or disclosure reaching S5.

quotes.text: For zero-shot benchmarking of off-the-shelf LLMs, we simply sample rollouts of the policy within the environment
Missed Local Management (Miss GP): Unnecessary escalation

rationale: Clinical terminal actions include treatment and referral, so the item applies. The paper identifies action types, makes clear they are sampled in a benchmark environment rather than clinical execution, and scores unsafe or unnecessary management actions; no S5 chunks are present.

quotes.text: We use GPT-5.4 as an automated judge to assign a binary score
Clinical equivalence allows synonymous wording and minor specificity differences

rationale: The grader inputs and method include predicted diagnosis/treatment strings, ground truth labels, terminal action, and LLM judgement. The paper gives a rationale for semantic judging, but does not validate on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates.

quotes.text: To prevent label leakage, we remove diagnostic statements and treatment recommendations from the clinical notes.

rationale: The paper reports a control against label leakage in clinical notes. It does not state that held-out labels are absent from every public surface, nor does it report canaries or provenance markers.

quotes.text: Table 2: Comparison of different metrics of Qwen2.5 (7B) optimized using GRPO and C-GRPO.
284 diagnose-and-manage and 201 abstain-and-refer cases

rationale: The benchmark reports results across named method/model partitions and gives slice sizes for the test split by management label. It has demographic fields but does not report model results by patient demographic subgroup.

quotes.text: The original clinical records were rigorously anonymized prior to any processing.
The accompanying evaluation code and scripts will be released under the Apache License 2.0.

rationale: The paper states the source as real clinical records and describes de-identification procedures. It also separates dataset terms from the code licence.
